name: Taiwo Oluwatobi Boluwatife
feedback: D1 is a complete catalogue. You captured all ten findings with the correct OWASP class, a CWE, and a verbatim evidence line for each: SQLi CWE-89 with the WHERE username concat, unsalted MD5 CWE-916, alg:none CWE-347 with the if alg === none return branch, no-expiry CWE-613, the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (you used CWE-321 which is a fine defensible variant of the 798 hardcoded-credential class), cookie flags CWE-614, open redirect CWE-601, path traversal CWE-22 at 02:24:02, stored XSS CWE-79 at 02:18:47, and XXE CWE-611. Critically you got the decoy right, naming the hash_equals signature comparison and proving it safe at the mechanism level because PHP guarantees constant-time comparison, and you correctly placed the real signature failure one branch above in the alg:none path rather than mislabelling alg:none as the decoy. D2 is strong: the chain runs in order, every hop carries a verbatim PoC, and you reconciled each hop to a capture line at 02:14:55, 02:15:31, 02:16:04, 02:18:47, 02:21:13 and 02:24:02 with the XXE as a parallel file-read route. You earned the senior-insight credit by tying the forged token to the shared /api/v1/internal service and using that to justify S:C on the alg:none vector. The one place you left points was the SQLi CVSS: you scored CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N at 7.5, and while you justified I:N honestly by saying you saw no captured modification, the login bypass that mints an admin session and the UNION extraction you describe do reach integrity, so the key vector is C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. The vector was complete and reasoned so I credited it nearly in full rather than halving it. Your impact work was exactly what was asked, 312 customers and a projected 63.0M naira from the 20-row sample mean of 202,011.62 with the linear-projection assumption stated plainly. D3 is near textbook: the executive summary is jargon-free and lands on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model names the Tor actor and the shared microservice, the findings table ties each bug to its evidence, the decoy is restated correctly, and the earliest-break fix is parameterizing the login query at the 02:15:31 hinge with alg:none named as the compulsory second cut. Your remediation table is ordered by risk reduced per hour and you said so explicitly, which is the effort-not-severity ordering the rubric rewards, and your two stopgaps give concrete fields, the username-parameter WAF regex with the apostrophe false-positive edge case handled, and the alg:none header detection keyed on the eyJhbGciOiJub25l prefix with a near-zero FP rationale. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canon II and Canon I by number and uses them load-bearing, and names NDPA 2023 Section 40 tied to the 312-customer export with the 72-hour Commission notification and the high-risk data-subject duty. I looked for any fabrication and found none, every figure and timestamp traces to the pack. The single most important fix is to revisit the SQLi CVSS integrity metric: when a bypass forges an authenticated admin session and enables UNION writes, score I:H not I:N, which moves that finding from 7.5 to roughly 9.1.
